title: Workers' council seeks Tk 32,000 wage as buyers hold back orders
excerpt: The council wants 12 arrested leaders freed. About 50 Gazipur factories and 28 in Savar and Ashulia are shut, and buyers want a quick end to unrest.

image.alt: Garment workers protesting over wages and holiday pay in Gazipur

content:
The Industrial Bangladesh Council (IBC) demanded a minimum wage of Tk 32,000 for garment workers at a press conference at the National Press Club on Thursday (19 November), The Business Standard reported. It also called for the release of 12 leaders and activists of its affiliated federations arrested since late October.

The current minimum wage is Tk 12,500. A wage board was formed on 1 November and factory owners are due to give their proposal on 23 November, The Daily Star reported.

Closures and buyers

Twenty-eight factories in Savar and Ashulia were closed under section 13(1) of the Labour Act, said Mohammad Mominul Islam Bhuiyan, superintendent of Industrial Police-1, and about 50 factories in Gazipur were shut indefinitely, said Md Amjad Hossain, superintendent of Gazipur Industrial Police, The Business Standard reported.

Buyers including H&M and Inditex met the BGMEA on 18 November and asked for a quick end to the unrest, The Daily Star reported, citing a BGMEA director. Many buyers are holding back autumn and winter orders.

Council general secretary Salauddin Swapn presented the demand. Senior vice-president Amirul Haque Amin called the wage proposal of the Centre for Policy Dialogue inadequate. The council also urged workers to go back to work while the wage board decides.

Why it matters

Arrests of union leaders and mass closures under section 13(1) of the Labour Act raise labour rights and civic space concerns. Lost wages hit workers' families quickly, and NGOs working in industrial areas on health, children and microfinance will feel it.

What to watch

The owners' proposal on 23 November, any release of the arrested leaders, and whether factories reopen.
